fields: Per-molecule quality filter for run-length analysis (minimum CpG calls and minimum methylation fraction required to count a molecule)
A chain rule, read from the sample's own molecules, that sets which molecules are counted: QUAL_MIN_CALLS 6, QUAL_MIN_METH 0.8.

It decides which molecules (reads) are counted toward the run-length instrument by requiring at least the stated number of calls and at least the stated methylation level; molecules that do not meet both are excluded before run lengths are tallied.

The run-length spectrum instrument (CP1 run lengths) needs this rule so that only molecules with enough calls and enough methylation feed into counting runs of lost marks; the row itself marks this as 'not the law: a chain rule', not a physical requirement of IAM's Law.
How it is obtained or computed

law_part records this as 'not the law: a chain rule', and lf_section confirms it is 'not part of IAM's Law'; it is a quality-control threshold applied to molecules, not a physical quantity entering IAM's Law.

fields: Expected run-length distribution under independent loss (null expectation for runs of unmethylated CpGs along a read, from that read's own loss rate)

The expected number of runs of lost marks of length 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or more along a single molecule, calculated from that molecule's own loss rate, used as the independent yardstick against which the actually observed run lengths are compared.

It supplies the 'independent' comparison baseline: each observed run of consecutive lost marks along a read is checked against this molecule-specific expectation to see whether the run is longer or shorter than chance placement alone would produce.

The instrument's job is to tell apart a slower crew producing scattered single losses from a double loss producing longer bare runs, and it can only make that call by comparing observed run lengths to this independent, per-molecule expectation.
How it is obtained or computed
Read from the sample's own molecules (source stage_q2_selfref, loss_runs): each molecule's own loss rate gives the independent expectation for runs of length 1-5+. Basis: statistics.

This is explicitly not part of IAM's Law (law_part: 'not the law: statistics (a yardstick)'; lf_section: 'not part of IAM's Law'). It is a statistical comparison quantity — a yardstick for judging run lengths — not a link or section of the Law itself.
Healthy value and how it is set

As an input it has no single fixed default: it is computed per molecule from that molecule's own loss rate, sourced from stage_q2_selfref (loss_runs) and read directly from the sample's own molecules rather than set to a fixed typical value.

Loss-run lengths 1-5+ against independence: the lengths of runs of lost marks along each molecule (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or more), each checked against what independent (random) placement of losses would predict.

Distinguishes a slower crew (scattered single losses) from a double loss (longer bare runs) by comparing observed counts of run lengths 1 through 5+ to their independent expectation; also tracked as held error by read length and by distance.

The instrument needs this to tell whether unmethylated stretches along a single read are arising as scattered single-site losses or as longer runs from losses occurring together, rather than assuming all loss is independent.
How it is obtained or computed

fields: Observed-over-expected ratio of unmethylated run lengths along single reads (runs of consecutive losses against independent placement)

The ratio of observed to expected run-lengths of consecutive lost (unmethylated) marks along single reads — lengths of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or more lost marks in a row, each compared against what independent, uncorrelated placement would predict.

It tells whether mark loss along a molecule looks like scattered single losses (a slower crew) or like longer bare runs (double loss), by comparing observed run lengths to their independent expectation.

The instrument needs this to distinguish the two ways marks can go missing along a read — scattered single losses versus longer runs of consecutive loss — which the row's job description frames as 'slower crew (scattered single losses) or double loss (longer bare runs)'.
How it is obtained or computed

Lengths of runs of lost marks along each molecule (1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or more) are each observed over its independent expectation; held error is also tracked by read length and by distance. fields: Held (unmethylated) error rate stratified by molecule length — one of the run-length instrument's checks of held error by read length

A tabulation of the held error (the fraction of marks found lost/unmethylated) broken out by the length of the molecule it was read on, produced as one button within the CP1 run-lengths instrument, which otherwise measures run lengths of lost marks along single reads against their independent expectation.

Reports held error separately for each molecule-length bin, to show whether held error changes with molecule length (healthy: flat). It is the CP1 instrument's held-error-by-read-length check; the instrument also reads held error by distance.

The instrument's job is to tell apart a slower crew (scattered single losses) from a double loss (longer bare runs); checking held error against molecule length is part of that same run-length accounting, done as a statistical yardstick rather than as part of IAM's Law.

records.name: Run lengths: how long the bare stretches run along one molecule
questions: Why not just one run-length ratio?
Single losses dominate the pool, so a single ratio missed planted runs of three; run excess by length sees them (2.42 -> 9.01).
Do healthy cells have random losses?
No: in the healthy test library runs of 3+ occur 2.4 times more often than independent placement, so the healthy bar must be measured, not assumed to be 1.
Is end damage counted as loss?
It is measured separately (excess loss at molecule ends) against the measured limit 0.002.
